A full-text index maps terms to the documents that contain them. The basic

search engines and by SQLite's FTS5 extension. For a query term q and document

## What quantisation does and does not buy

Weight-only quantisation reduces checkpoint size and the memory needed to hold
weights. It does not automatically make CPU inference faster. A naive
implementation dequantises the weight matrix on every forward pass, which adds
computation and can be slower than float32 matrix multiplication. Real speedups
require fused integer kernels, which is why the honest claim for a simple
implementation is "smaller checkpoint, measured accuracy delta" rather than
"faster".

Activations stay in floating point in this scheme. Quantising activations

Large models are often trained with a structured chat template that the serving

A float32 parameter costs four bytes. A 49 million parameter model therefore
needs about 196 MB for its weights alone. Quantising weights to eight bits

four bits reduce it to about 25 MB. For a model that must run offline on a
laptop, checkpoint size and memory bandwidth are often the binding constraints,

A decoder-only transformer is a stack of identical blocks operating on a

# The decoder-only transformer used by TinyLM-50

## Blocks and the residual stream

A decoder-only transformer is a stack of identical blocks operating on a
residual stream of shape (batch, sequence, hidden). Each block applies two
sub-layers, each preceded by normalisation and followed by a residual
addition. Pre-norm placement, where the normalisation is applied to the input
of the sub-layer rather than its output, is easier to train at depth because
the identity path from input to output is never rescaled.

TinyLM-50 uses RMSNorm. RMSNorm divides by the root mean square of the
activations and multiplies by a learned per-feature weight. It omits mean
subtraction, which saves a little work and performs comparably to LayerNorm in
this setting. Computation is done in float32 internally", "citations": [{"title": "The decoder-only transformer used by TinyLM-50", "path": "transformer_architecture.md", "chunk": 0, "start_char": 0, "end_char": 796}]}

# The decoder-only transformer used by TinyLM-50

## Blocks and the residual stream

A decoder-only transformer is a stack of identical blocks operating on a
residual stream of shape (batch, sequence, hidden). Each block applies two
sub-layers, each preceded by normalisation and followed by a residual
addition. Pre-norm placement, where the normalisation is applied to the input
of the sub-layer rather than its output, is easier to train at depth because
the identity path from input to output is never rescaled.

TinyLM-50 uses RMSNorm. RMSNorm divides by the root mean square of the
activations and multiplies by a learned per-feature weight. It omits mean
subtraction, which saves a little work and performs comparably to LayerNorm in
this setting. Computation is done in float32 internally", "citations": [{"title": "The decoder-only transformer used by TinyLM-50", "path": "transformer_architecture.md", "chunk": 0, "start_char": 0, "end_char": 796}]}

# BM25 ranking and SQLite FTS5

## What full-text search needs

A full-text index maps terms to the documents that contain them. The basic
structure is an inverted index: for every term, a posting list of document ids,
term frequencies and positions. At query time the engine looks up each query
term, intersects or unions the posting lists, and ranks the candidates.

Ranking matters because a term like "the" appears everywhere while a rare term
is informative. BM25 (Best Matching 25) is the ranking function used by most
search engines and by SQLite's FTS5 extension. For a query term q and document
d it combines three signals:

- term frequency: more occurrences of q in d increase the score, with
  diminishing returns controlled by the parameter k1;
- inverse document frequency: terms that", "citations": [{"title": "BM25 ranking and SQLite FTS5", "path": "bm25_and_fts5.md", "chunk": 0, "start_char": 0, "end_char": 798}]}

## Blocks and the residual stream

A decoder-only transformer is a stack of identical blocks operating on a
residual stream of shape (batch, sequence, hidden). Each block applies two
sub-layers, each preceded by normalisation and followed by a residual
addition. Pre-norm placement, where the normalisation is applied to the input

the identity path from input to output is never rescaled.
